clusters.pick_reason: 2692's settlement path groups outstanding request ids by stream (needed because a batched POST maps several ids to one stream/response) and reuses an id's real response if one already arrived, instead of overwriting it — 2600's version answers with a single flat 404 for the whole pending response, which would clobber already-resolved ids in a batched request. 2692 also settles with a JSON-RPC-level error (-32000 'Connection closed') matching the JSON-RPC error envelope clients expect, versus 2600's HTTP-level 404. Note 2600 additionally retires the _requestToStreamMapping correlation table to fix a separate leak (stale correlation causing send() to resolve against a retired request after storeEvent()'s await) that 2692 does not address; that fix is not covered by 2692's diff and should be re-filed or folded in separately if still present on main.

clusters.pick_reason: 2692's settlement path groups outstanding request ids by stream (needed because a batched POST maps several ids to one stream/response) and reuses an id's real response if one already arrived, instead of overwriting it — 2600's version answers with a single flat 404 for the whole pending response, which would clobber already-resolved ids in a batched request. 2692 also settles with a JSON-RPC-level error (-32000 'Connection closed') matching the JSON-RPC error envelope clients expect, versus 2600's HTTP-level 404. Note 2600 additionally retires the _requestToStreamMapping correlation table to fix a separate leak (stale correlation causing send() to resolve against a retired request after storeEvent()'s await) that 2692 does not address; that fix is not covered by 2692's diff and should be re-filed or folded in separately if still present on main.
